neighbours.label: ' the' right after a verb of crossing or traversing (crossed the river, crossing the Chasm)
fire: After weeks of travel the pioneers finally crossed the mountains.
Every spring the herds cross the plains in search of grass.
Our ferry slowly crossed the channel in thick fog.
Two climbers traversed the glacier before sunrise.
Legend says the army forded the stream at night.
The migrating birds cross the Sahara twice a year.
In 1927 Lindbergh flew across the Atlantic alone.
The refugees waded across the shallow river at dusk.
quiet: After weeks of travel the pioneers finally rested in the mountains.
Every spring the herds graze on fresh grass near home.
Our ferry slowly docked in thick fog.
Two climbers photographed the glacier before sunrise.
Legend says the army camped by the stream at night.
The migrating birds rest in Morocco twice a year.
In 1927 Lindbergh became famous for his flight.
The refugees waited near the shallow river at dusk.
